headline: Quantum Limits: From Error Control to Fundamental Bounds
summary: Today's selection bridges rigorous theoretical limits with practical NISQ and network engineering. Key theoretical results establish exact thresholds for state spectrum estimation and thermal entanglement decay alongside new non-Abelian LDPC codes. Meanwhile, applied efforts optimize portfolio finance, network routing policies, and dynamical decoupling sequences on real quantum processors.

themes.title: Fundamental Limits & Error Correction
themes.body: Theoretical bounds on quantum resources: establishing optimal copy complexity for spectrum estimation, sharp thermal death thresholds for entanglement, and non-Abelian sheaf qLDPC codes with linear distance.

themes.title: Hardware Control & NISQ Applications
themes.body: Addressing physical hardware constraints through sparse dynamical decoupling sequences on 127 qubits, and encoding 1500-variable portfolio optimization problems into variational circuits.

themes.title: Quantum Network Optimization
themes.body: Leveraging deep reinforcement learning and message passing networks to efficiently schedule simultaneous entanglement requests across distributed quantum systems.

connections.body: Both papers establish tight, provably optimal bounds for core quantum phenomena: one resolves the copy complexity of state spectrum learning, while the other derives the exact critical temperature where entanglement strictly vanishes.
